observations: The page number «82» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01 continues the sentence that ends p. 81 (JP2 0113, L36), «die der Zahl 31 in der Kolonne Anni». L02, L05, L28: «29d 0h 14m 46s», «8h 48m 7s», «7h 49m», the letters raised.

L21-L26: the computation, set as a table of five columns divided by vertical rules, which are not transcribed: the heads «Dies et horae» (in one line, set between the two lines of the other heads), «Longit. media solis et lunae», «Anomalia lunae», «Argumentum latitud. lunae» (in two lines); the names joined to the figures by dotted leaders (L24-L25), which are not transcribed; in L23 and L26 the figures with their units, in L24-L25 without; L26 below a rule across the table, broken at the vertical rules. L30-L34: the true places of the sun and the moon, set in two halves of a table, each half with its names at the left and its figures in a column, the names of L33 joined to the figures by dotted leaders, not transcribed, and a rule under the figures of L33. Each printed row is one line here, the cells separated by our «|»; the empty cells give the columns room and are not printed.

L21-L28. Checked: 29d 2h 4m 51s + 5h 43m 50s = 29d 7h 48m 41s; 123° 49′ 42″ + 177° 30′ 35″ = 301° 20′ 17″; 252° 31′ 18″ + 226° 38′ 40″ = 479° 9′ 58″, less 360° 119° 9′ 58″ (note 4); 30° 19′ 50″ + 136° 48′ 10″ = 167° 8′ 0″. 270 + 17 years end with the year 287, so that 0 Muḥarram 288 is the radix of the year; counted from Thursday 15 July 622 (p. 39, JP2 0071), noon of 29 Muḥarram 288 is 22 January 901, a Thursday, and the mean conjunction 7h 49m later the evening of 22 January, as L18-L19 say.

L01-L05 and L21-L24. Checked against Brahmagupta's synodic month, 1 577 916 450 000 days in 53 433 300 000 months (29.5305821 days, see p. 42, JP2 0074): 360 months exceed 30 Arab years (10631 days) by 13m 44s, so that from the row of 31 to the row of 271 the time to the next conjunction grows by 8 × 13m 44s = 1h 49m 53s, against 29d 2h 4m 51s − 29d 0h 14m 46s = 1h 50m 5s of the tables; 204 months exceed the 17 years 1-17 (6024 days) by 5h 43m 47s (L24: 5h 43m 50s); 12 months exceed one common year of 354 days by 8h 48m 27s, against the 8h 48m 7s of L05, to be compared with Table 71. The true new moon of January 901 fell in the morning of 23 January (about 7.4h Terrestrial Time; Meeus's algorithm), the day of al-Battānī's solar eclipse (L15-L16).

L30-L34 and N06-N07. Checked: 301° 20′ 17″ − 77° 55′ = 223° 25′ 17″, and 301° 20′ 17″ + 1° 30′ 39″ = 302° 50′ 56″ (the solar anomaly greater than 180°, the equation added); 301° 20′ 17″ − 4° 15′ 45″ = 297° 4′ 32″ (the lunar anomaly less than 180°, the equation subtracted). The rule sin q = sin 2° 14′ · sin m gives for the sun 1° 32′ 7″ and sin q = sin 4° 56′ · sin m for the moon 4° 18′ 26″ (see p. 46, JP2 0078), more than the 1° 30′ 39″ and 4° 15′ 45″ read in Tables 25 and 24; to be compared with the tables.

L18: «Muḥarram» in italics with the dot under the ḥ; L23-L28: «Muḥarram», «Muḥ.» upright in the table and in L28. L15: «im 30. Kapitel», the chapter of al-Battānī (note 2). Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Batt.», «Schiaparelli», «Nallino»; italics: «collecti», «Signa», «Notae», «Beispiel», «Muḥarram» (L18, N01), «Konjunktion», «Neumond».

The dashes: L05 «7s. — Die», the long dash with a space on either side; L20 «69—72» and L29 «21—26», the long dash set close (48 px); N02 «56—57» and N03 «228—229», the long dash of the small type (27 and 42 px).
The colons, semicolons and the question mark stand after the thin space of the edition (9-14 px measured; «288 :» in L26, 11 px; «stattgefunden ?», 9 px).
